name: Shin-Koenji
tagline: Shinjuku in 12 minutes and Shibuya in 22 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Suginami City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 31 minutes to Otemachi, 12 minutes to Shinjuku, 22 minutes to Shibuya and 43 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 43 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 6.7 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 43 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 38 m to 44.7 m, a difference of 6.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 2 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 23 clinics and 16 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 北條病院, about 11 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 静山会清川病院, about 13 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line runs at 154% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 新大塚→茗荷谷, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. 1LDK ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the lowest in the 23 wards. a small projected flood depth pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Koenji is ahead on rail connections and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shin-Koenji. Koenji also has the JR Chuo Rapid Line and JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local), which Shin-Koenji does not. With more lines, Koenji is the better connected of the two. To Tokyo, for instance, Koenji is 6 minutes quicker. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Higashi-Koenji; for lower rent, Shin-Koenji.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shin-Koenji. It is served by the same lines as Shin-Koenji. To Shibuya, for instance, Higashi-Koenji is 3 minutes quicker. A one-room flat costs about ¥6,000 more at Higashi-Koenji. On how easy the shopping is, Shin-Koenji comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 9 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the lowest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
